attributes.action: Reform e-petitions: lower thresholds, stop closures, create direct path to law
attributes.additional_details: The e-petitions system is a dead-end. 10,000 signatures gets a copy-paste reply; 100,000 gets a non-binding debate the Government can ignore. High thresholds suppress citizen legislation. The Committee can reject petitions unchecked. We propose: no closure unless three independent experts unanimously certify it is physically impossible or outside UK powers. Lower thresholds and make top petitions become binding Public Bills for a mandatory Commons vote.
attributes.background: Reform the e-petitions system. Lower the 10,000 and 100,000 thresholds. Ban arbitrary closures unless three independent experts certify a petition is physically impossible or outside UK jurisdiction. Make petitions hitting the top threshold become binding Public Bills for a mandatory Commons vote.

rejection.details: Unclear - the petition is not clear on how the text of a petition becomes a bill, what happens when the petition is about a subject on which a bill would not be legally appropriate or effective, what expertise the experts are supposed to have and in what way they are supposed to be independent - nor is it clear what new thresholds should apply.
